Unfortunately, they only appear twice in the show disappear from the story soon afterThe Desertseemingly replaced by Azula who was already pursuing both parties anyway. They get slightly more prominence in the comics. Absurdly Sharp Blade: Kahchi's halberd can easily cut through stone statues. Alliterative Name: TheRoughRhinos. Ambiguously Brown: Ogodei has a darker skin tone than several other characters.

characters.name: The Southern Raiders
characters.description: Animal Motifs: Sea ravens, being the symbol on their banners and their helmets resembling birds. Curb-Stomp Battle: Katara takes care of them pretty easily in the modern day. Custom Uniform: Their uniforms are more unique than other Fire Nation units, with their helmets having a bird theme. Fragile Speedster: Their ships are much smaller and faster than the usual Fire Nation ones, making them more suited to coastal raids. Hollywood Tactics: Subverted. It looks like they're playing this trope straight by charging straight at the Southern Water Tribe warriors, but it's a distraction to allow their commander to sneak into the village and find the last waterbender.

characters.name: Current Commander
characters.description: Curb-Stomp Cushion: He lasts longer than the rest of his men put together against Katara and Zuko. No Name Given: It's unclear what his name is. Rank Up: He was presumably promoted after his predecessor's retirement.

characters.name: Yon Rha
characters.description: Abusive Parents: From what little is seen of his mother, she's shown to be a shrewish, ungrateful, verbally abusive woman. According to the writers, her treatment of him after the war grounded Yon Rha down from a terrifying monster of a man to the miserable wretch he is in the present. Alas, Poor Villain: Katara will never forgive Yon Rha for murdering her mother, but she realizes that he's too pitiful and pathetic to even warrant her vengeance. She almost feels disappointed by this revelation since she really wants to kill him as the evil man she once remembered. Basement Dweller: After retiring as commander of the Southern Raiders he became a browbeaten shadow of his former self due to being forced to live with his verbally abusive mother. Break the Haughty: He's become a shadow of his former self after he retired from the Fire Nation Military, living with his mean mother, having an unpleasant life and overall looking miserable. When Katara realizes this, she can't bring herself to kill him, so she just leaves him to his pitiful existence, at which point he breaks down crying. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: Zigzagged. When Katara first encounters him again years after he murdered her mother, she asks him if he knows her. When he admits he doesn't recognize her, she threatens him, and it's enough to jog his memory of the little Water Tribe girl he fleetingly encountered six years ago. Since he remembers the rest of what happened that day, hisexpressionsays it all.

characters.name: Combustion Man
characters.description: A mysterious assassin hired by Zuko to hunt down and kill the Avatar. Relentless in his pursuit of Aang and seemingly unstoppable, he uses a unique form of Firebending by shooting laser beams that causeStuff Blowing Up. Also known as Sparky Sparky Boom Man. Achilles' Heel: Getting hit in the tattoo on his head screws up the flow of chi which creates his explosions, causing them to blow up in his face. All There in the Manual: His unique form of firebending, combustion bending, isn't given a proper name until Book 3 ofThe Legend of Korra. Appropriated Appellation: Both of his names were made up by Sokka for the sake of identification. Combustion Man never hears them and it's unknown what he calls himself. Zuko apparently knows his real name, but never gets a chance to say it. Artificial Limbs: According to the writers, Combustion Man blew off his right hand and leg by accident while experimenting with his powers that's why he's since replaced them with metal prosthetics. Unusually, they are rather functional, as Combustion Man can casually shatter ice and claw through stone with his metal arm, and he also once used them as a shield to block Katara's attacks.

characters.name: Jee
characters.description: The ranking officer on board Zuko's ship. Bring It: When Zuko challenges him, he accepts with no fear. The Dragon: He could be considered the closest thing Zuko had at his most villainous in Season 1, since he's the highest ranking member of the crew besides Zuko and Iroh (who is more of a mentor and rarely takes part in Zuko's conflicts). Everyone Has Standards: He is genuinely shocked to hear what Zuko's father did to him, and it gives him a much greater respect and sympathy for Zuko's motivations. A Father to His Men: His concern for the crew leads to his argument with Zuko. He also risks his life along with Zuko to rescue the helmsman from falling to his death.

characters.name: Shoji
characters.description: I Am Spartacus: He's the first of many students to put on a headband like Aang's to keep the headmaster from catching him (albeit over a party he threw rather than because they know he's the Avatar). Jaw Drop: He gets one upon seeing Aang use earthbending powers as he leaves. Nice Guy: Shoji comes across as a normal kid who's nice to a new student and enjoys carefree activities, which he invites Aang to participate in.

characters.name: On Ji
characters.description: Allegorical Character: She's a noteworthy example of how the people of the Fire Nation can sometimes be friendly, openminded, and even good natured people despite being associated with Hide, who represents unthinkingly loyal and aggressive military officers. Ambiguous Situation: Whether she's actually in a relationship with Hide isn't made crystal clear. He could beentitledSelf-Proclaimed Love Interestto her, but she never explicitly denies it, making it possible she did agree to date Hide in the past. Either way, On Ji's visible annoyance with his nasty, territorial behavior towards other boys, her very clear interest in Aang as "Kuzon", and her not bringing him to the secret dance party make it clear that, either way, she doesn't like Hide and doesn't want to be a couple the same way he does. Girl Next Door: She is friendly, wholesome, and cute, and technically became a childhood friend of Aang's since both were still children when they met. Luminescent Blush: When Aang, who is disguised as "Kuzon", offers his hand in the crowd of students during the secret dance party, On Ji visibly blushes shyly when taking his hand and going to dance. She does show that she has a crush on him. Nice Girl: She warns Aang about not getting caught by the Headmaster regarding Momo, and confirms she's not a tattletale. She keeps her promise not to snitch on him.

characters.name: Hide
characters.description: Allegorical Character: He's a star example of what the Fire Nation school system could produce: A muscular build and a weak mind, being destined to grow up to become a strict Fire Nation military officer who would be hated by his subordinates. Ambiguous Situation: Whether he's actually in a relationship with On Ji isn't made crystal clear. He could beentitledSelf-Proclaimed Love Interestto her, but she never explicitly denies it, making it possible she did agree to date Hide in the past. Either way, On Ji's visible annoyance with his nasty, territorial behavior towards other boys, her very clear interest in Aang as "Kuzon", and her not bringing him to the secret dance party make it clear that, either way, she doesn't like Hide or the idea of being an couple the same way he does. The Bully: He antagonizes everyone at school and uses his position as a star student to do what he wants without consequence. Crazy Jealous Guy: Anyone who gets near On Ji while he's around will earn his wrath. Dirty Coward: He has no problems with using his good standing with the Headmaster and pulling aWounded Gazelle Gambitto get other students in trouble if he couldn't beat them up himself.

characters.name: Ozai
characters.description: Ruler of the Fire Nation and likely the most powerful Firebender on the planet, Ozai isthe main antagonistof the series. A ruthless warlord and megalomaniac, Ozai is willing to burn the rest of the world to the ground so he can rule. He has little to no empathy for anyone, including his own children (though he acts decently towards them if they prove themselves useful). Aang must defeat Ozai before Ozai can harness Sozin's Comet and use it tobring the war to a permanent end. 0% Approval Rating: From the glimpses we get at Fire Nation soldiers' and citizens' conversations, it's clear that most are more loyal to the title of "Fire Lord" than to Ozai as a person. The Yu Yan archers use the term "Fire Lord propaganda" derisively, and their General regards his and Zhao's hunt for the Avatar as out-of-touch with the ground troops fighting the real war. Outside of the mainland, the people indigenous to the Earth Kingdom colonies (outside of a few individuals) don't respect him OR his title. It says something when Zuko is permitted to take the throne while Ozai is still technically alive. It's not technicallyzero, because the New Ozai Society forms in effort to place him back on the throne; but they're a decidedly fringe group, and even they're more interested in restoring the Empire than in Ozai himself. Above Good and Evil: He believes that the will of the Fire Lord is the be-all and end-all of what's right and wrong. Absolute Xenophobe: While he primarily targets the earthbenders for his genocidal plans, in reality, he's hateful towardsanyone, bender or not, for no such reason other than insane pettiness. Abusive Parents: One of the most notable examples in animation history, and it's allPlayed for Horror. Ozai isnightmarishlybrutal and cruel to both of his children no matter how hard either of them works to earn his approval, and he actively encourages their worst traits so he can use them asTyke Bombs—allwithout an iota of compassion or remorse. Zuko even describes him

characters.name: Lu Ten
characters.description: Iroh's only son, who like his father served in the Fire Nation army, and died during the siege of Ba Sing Se, prompting Iroh's withdrawal from the city, his retirement from the army, and hisHeel–Face Turn. It also provoked Ozai's grab for the throne and everything that followed. The Ace: Not to the extent of his father, but nevertheless, Lu Ten was a very talented Firebender with a gifted intellect, which earned him praise fromFire Lord Azulon himself, who allowed his eldest grandson considerable freedom, This resulted in Lu Ten growing up far from the pressures of the royal family, unlike his cousins. Big Brother Mentor: Is implied to have been this to Zuko. A brief flashback to Zuko's childhood sees him being tended to by Iroh and Lu Ten. Cheerful Child: He was one, judging by Iroh's memories of him playing at firebending. Fatal Flaw: His curiosity and his trust in his father Iroh. He was never content to stay home and be safe when he could be out learning and experiencing the world, and the only reason he didn't fully clock that the Fire Nation were the bad guys despite his intelligence and free-thinking nature is because he trusted that Iroh would always do the right thing- only Iroh wasalsoblinded by Fire Nation propaganda and genuinely believed the war was righteous. For this reason, Lu Ten served under his father in the Siege of Ba Sing Se, putting him in the position to be killed in battle.

characters.name: Sozin
characters.description: Sozin is the man responsible for the destruction of the Air Nomads, father to Azulon, grandfather to Iroh and Ozai, and great-grandfather to Zuko, Azula, and Lu Ten. As Fire Lord during Roku's era, Sozin plotted to take over the world as a way of sharing the Fire Nation's prosperity with everyone. Knowing that the Avatar would oppose his plans, he used the power of a passing comet to launch a devastating first strike on the Air Nomads, wiping them out (except Aang, who he missed) and leaving him free to wage a one hundred year war. Although he is now long dead, his comet will return to allow his grandsonOzaito do the same for the rest of the world. Absurdly Elderly Father: When he died Sozin was 102 years old while his son Azulon was 20 when he became Fire Lord, meaning that Sozin was 82 years old when he fathered his son Azulon. It is implied that he conceived children with multiple women/concubines to sire, to his standards, the ideal heir, since it is confirmed that Sozin favored Azulon over "another relative". The Ace: Whatever else you can say about him, he was undeniably an extraordinary Fire Bender - he's the only Fire Bender we see besides his grandson Iroh (who is probably the most skilled fire bender of his time) who doesn't merely bend fire, but heat. AndIrohusually does itwith tea.Sozin did itwith a volcano. Alas, Poor Villain: His narration from the end of his life makes it clear that he spent his dying days being haunted by how much brighter his younger days from before he and Roku fell out were, and how he spent most of his life on a fruitless journey after the Air Nomad genocide failing to find the next Avatar. It's overall hinted that Sozin realized by the very end thathe'd wasted his life by betraying his best friend and bringing much more harm than good to the world, which was the opposite of what he'd originally set out to do. The fact that everyone in the Fire Nation believes after Sozin's death that he died a very victorious man makes the reali

characters.name: Zeisan
characters.description: Badass Normal: A non-bender who did everything she could to stop her brother, even learning chi-blocking as a fighting technique. Cain and Abel: The Abel to Sozin's Cain. Family Theme Naming: Continues the trend of people in the Fire Nation Royal family having a strong "Z" sound in their names. Good Counterpart: To Azula. Both are the Princesses of the Fire Nation, but while Azula worked under Ozai to conquer the world, Zeisan worked to undermine the war started by her brother. Has a Type: Has had romantic feelings for two of her tutors. Both were very skilled women who had a different way of thinking from the usual Fire Nation royalty and nobility.

characters.name: Azulon
characters.description: Azulon was the Fire Lord before Ozai, son of Sozin, father to Iroh and Ozai, and grandfather to Zuko, Azula, and Lu Ten. Famed for his military prowess and skill at firebending, he ruled the Fire Nation with an iron grip. He was a man with little warmth in him, sentencing men to death with a stunning callousness. Ozai seemed to have had as strained a relationship with him as he did with his own son, always seeking to earn his favor but always being met with scorn. After Ozai tried his patience one time too many, making an inappropriate bid for the throne, Azulon ordered Zuko's death, to teach his son a lesson in humility. He died shortly after giving that order, making way for Ozai to succeed him as Fire Lord. Absurdly Elderly Father: It's subtle, but his eldest son Iroh was in his 50s at his oldest when Azulon was in his mid 90s, while his second son Ozai is about a decade younger, meaning Azulon had Ozai in his 50s. Abusive Parents: He ordered Ozai to kill Zuko so he would know what it is like to lose a son. Ozai later admits that he would have actually gone through with it if Ursa hadn't intervened. It's left ambiguous if he carried on this fromhisfather, Sozin, or if he just came by it on his own. The Ace: He was an accomplished general for the Fire Nation, turned the army more efficient, leading to numerous conquests and led the Fire Nation for the majority of the Hundred Year War. Furthermore, Azulon was considered one of the best firebenders in the world with no one daring to cross him and is remembered as one of the Fire Nations strongest and most efficient leaders. Ambiguous Situation: Much of his actual character and even his actions are fairly ambiguous. The only knowledge we have of him and his actions (besides Zuko's memories) comes from two in-universe sources, neither of whom is bound byVillains Never Lie.

characters.name: Player Aang
characters.description: Player Aang is an athletic young woman wearing a bald cap. She plays Aang as hyperactive and excessively outgoing, with a penchant for playing pranks on people. Player Aang's mission as the Avatar is to bring "joy and fun" to the World. Player Aang triggers the Avatar State by saying "Avatar State, yip-yip!" Real Aangis dismayed to seethat Player Aang is a woman. He is even more dismayed when Player Ozai kills Player Aang at the end. Adaptational Wimp: Is never seen water- or firebending (and only earthbends once to chuck small rocks at Player Azula) and is no match for Ozai boosted by Sozin's Comet. While the real Aang was on the back foot for most of that fight until he accidentally unlocked his chakra, he still did put up a fight. Affably Evil: He's seen as "evil" by the Fire Nation audience, but also funny and lovable. Affectionate Parody: Of the Broadway adaptation ofPeter Pan, right down to using a female actress to play a young male and using wires to simulate flying. Even the way she talks sounds like Mary Martin playing Peter. Big "NO!"/Slow "NO!": A good eight seconds long when Ozai burns her.

characters.name: Player Katara
characters.description: Player Katara is older and fatter than Real Katara, and not as beautiful. She speaks in a much huskier voice than the real Katara. Player Katara is melodramatic, prone to crying on any occasion, obsessed with hope, and does not fight. She wears her heart on her sleeve, especially in front of Player Aang. Player Katara is in love with Player Zuko, and regards Player Aang as her little brother. Adaptational Curves: She's more curvaceous than the real Katara. Adaptational Skimpiness: Player Katara's wardrobe lacks the real one's warming clothes, resulting in her showing some skin due to the low neckline and leg slit. The real Katara didn't start wearing skin-baring clothes until she went to the Fire Nation in Book 3. Adaptational Villainy: The real Katara was utterly horrified when Jet destroyed an Earth Kingdom town, and immediately turned on him. Player Katara, however, is impressed by how "bad" Jet is. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: Pu-on Tim certainly screwed up with Katara's romantic preferences.While Kataradidhave a crush on Jet, she lost it as soon as she realized that he wanted to destroy a town, and when they next met in Ba Sing Se, she attacked him on sight. This Katara is charmed by Jet's terrorism, and by the next time they're shown interacting, Jet is already brainwashed into insanity.Player Katara repeatedly says that she sees Aang as like "a little brother." The only time Katara says anything similar, it was inThe Fortuneteller, and it's implied she started seeing him as a potential romantic partner (instead of "a cute little guy, like Momo") by the end of the episode, when Sokka inadvertently reminds her that Aunt Wu's prophecy of her marrying a powerful bender could easily apply to Aang (being the Avatar, he'sthemost powerful bender).Player Katara flirts with Zuko in the caves under Ba Sing Se. In reality, while their discussion was certainly tender and vulnerable, it wasn't really romantic- and then of course Zuko almost immediately blew all his go

characters.name: Player Sokka
characters.description: Player Sokka is much older than Real Sokka, with buck teeth. He's a backwoods, dumb-muscle, Water Tribe hick, and the comic relief. Player Sokka is constantly hungry, and obsessed with eating meat. But the actor for Player Sokka is a pretty chill guy — when Sokka approaches him backstage with some ideas for new jokes, the actor gladly incorporates them into the scene, despite initial misgivings — ("Oh, boy, another fan with "Ideas"") and to the delight of the audience. Adaptational Dumbass: Lacks the real Sokka's brains. Big Eater: He's always hungry and wanting to eat. Only Yue's death can take his mind off food. Catchphrase: "I'm starving!" He says it twice in the first 30 seconds of the play. Character Exaggeration: Of Sokka's tendency to focus on food and hisPlucky Comic Reliefstatus.

characters.name: Player Toph
characters.description: Player Toph is a big, burly man who is blind but can "see" using echolocation, emitting a loud scream. Real Toph likes Player Toph, saying "I wouldn't have cast it any other way." Actually Pretty Funny: More Actually Pretty Awesome, but Toph was the only one who genuinely liked how she was portrayed in the play without doing so begrudgingly even. Adaptational Curves:Played for Laughs. This version of Toph is very buff compared to the actual one who is a scrawnylittle girl. She finds the change amusing though. Adaptational Superpower Change: He uses Echolocation (read: screaming in people's faces) to compensate for his blindness instead of Seismic Sense which the real Toph uses. The Big Guy: Except that unlike the real Toph, he isliterallythe big guy of the group.

characters.name: Player Zuko
characters.description: Player Zuko is more accurate than other Players, but Real Zuko considers Player Zuko too stiff and dour, and Player Zuko's scar is on the wrong side. Player Zuko is even more obsessed with honor and capturing the Avatar than the real Zuko, and shouts "honor!" more than he says anything else. He flirts with Player Katara. In Act III, he is killed by Player Azula for his betrayal of the Fire Nation. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: There's no indication he's ever in a relationship with Player Mai, and he instead is teased with Katara. Anime Hair: The play's third act sees him sporting aVegeta-esque head of spiky hair. Big, Stupid Doodoo-Head: During hisIgnored Epiphanynear the end of Act II, he tells Player Iroh that he smells and that he hates him for all time. Character Exaggeration: The real Zuko is understandably hell-bent on getting his honor back, but Player Zuko is outright obsessed by it.

characters.name: Player Iroh
characters.description: Player Iroh is Player Zuko's doddering glutton of an uncle. He is obsessed with cake instead of tea, and is trying and failing to give Player Zuko cake. Player Iroh is betrayed and defeated by Player Zuko, which is uncomfortably close to the truth for Zuko. Adaptational Villainy: The play is Fire Nation propaganda after all. Naturally, Iroh's not going to be played in a positive light. The real Iroh acts against his brother's regime both because he respects the other Nations and because heloveshis country, and wants to redeem it. This version just thinks treachery is fun and is notably associated with an Earth Kingdom flag. Adaptational Wimp: The real Iroh is a firebender powerful enough to keep up with the other members of the Royal Family and a talented martial artist. Player Iroh neither firebends nor fights. Big Eater: Unlike the real Iroh, who loves tea, Player Iroh loves cake instead, which makes him look more hedonistic. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Justlook at them. They're probably fake, but still.

characters.name: Player Azula
characters.description: Player Azula is older than Real Azula, with a huskier voice, and wears pink, along with thick makeup and long painted nails. Player Azula electrocutes Player Aang at the end of Act II, then kills Player Zuko in Act III. Abled in the Adaptation: She fights and defeats Player Zuko while in a right state of mind. During the eventualFinal Battle, the real Azula issuffering a nasty case ofSanity Slippage, which costs her the victory. Adaptational Heroism: The play is Fire Nation propaganda, so of course it presents Azula in a better light than the show does. She doesn't shoot Iroh in the adaption ofThe Chase, she's motivated by patriotism instead of Ozai's approval (which is reflected in the scene where Zuko chooses her over Iroh; in the play she asks him to choose "your nation" instead of treachery, while in reality she saidthat Ozai wanted him back), and she doesn't bully Zuko, only acting against him after he defects to join the Avatar. The Bad Guy Wins: Unlike the real Azula, she kills Player Zuko. Combat Stilettos: As opposed to her real counterpart, who constantly wears sensible flat-soled boots.

characters.name: Player Ozai
characters.description: Player Ozai is the Fire Lord in the play. As the play is propaganda, Player Ozai is a heroic leader, and he looks much more like the real Ozai than any of the Players look like their characters. In the climax of Act III, he kills Player Aang with the power of Sozin's Comet and conquers the World. Abled in the Adaptation: The play ends with Ozai killing Aang. The actualFinal Battleends with Aang defeating Ozai and removing his bending. Adaptational Heroism: He wants to take over the world and kill Player Aang, but unlike the real Ozai, he has no plans of genocide. He also embarks on his conquest to live up to his ancestors' legacy and not because he's a completely self-serving scumbag. Adaptational Modesty: He fights and defeats Player Aang fully clothed. During the eventualFinal Battle, the real Ozai is in aShirtless Scene. Adaptational Nice Guy: He implicitly burned his son's face and isn't too choked up about said son dying, but the play doesn't frame that as abuse because Player Zuko is aVillain Protagonistwho betrays his nation and deservedly dies for it. There's also no evidence that he's emotionally abusive to Player Azula, particularly during the lead-up to Sozin's Comet where his toxic treatment of her real counterpart would come to a tipping point.

characters.name: Player Mai
characters.description: Player Mai looks similar to real Mai, albeit with a few differences. Her belt has a sad face on it, her fringe covers her eyes, and she keeps her knives in her "ox horn" hair. Action Girl: Like the real deal, she's a knife master and one of Azula's elite henchmen. Anime Hair: Her odango hair is exaggerated to the point where she can stick knives in it. Beauty Inversion: The real Mai is quite beautiful, even cute, in her own way. Player Mai, not so much. Blush Sticker: Due to the exaggerated makeup the female actresses are wearing.

characters.name: Player Ty Lee
characters.description: Player Ty Lee is a pudgy ballerina. Instead of doing acrobatic stunts, she dances sedately across the stage. Instead of chi-blocking by poking people, she kisses them. Acrofatic: Downplayed. While she still defeats enemy soldiers, she dances quite lazily across the stage thanks to her being overweight with a big gut that prevents her from doing too much. Action Girl: She's one of Azula's elite henchmen, and is shown defeating a soldier in one hit with herKiss of Death. Adaptational Curves: Much fatter than the real Ty Lee who is slender and athletic. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: She has the same sort of outfit as Ty Lee to sell her as a pretty, enticing young woman who uses kisses in combat, though it comes across as more funny than anything since this Ty Lee has a big belly that's left completely on display thanks to it.

characters.name: Player Suki
characters.description: Player Suki looks very close to the real Suki, but her headdress and fans are exaggerated. She has no lines. In Act I, she trains Player Sokka in the ways of the Kyoshi Warriors. Action Girl: Teaches Sokka how to be a Kyoshi warrior. Amazon Brigade: The Kyoshi warriors are all female. Battle Ballgown: Her uniform. Cool Mask: Her kabuki makeup.

characters.name: Player Bumi
characters.description: Player Bumi is the King of Omashu. He wears a padded suit to simulate the real Bumi's muscles, an oversized monocle to look like Bumi'sMad Eye, and a feathered hat as a crown, which looks like Bumi's pet Flopsy. Player Bumi speaks in rhymes. Adaptational Curves: While his real life counterpart was certainly buff, this version of Bumi is a lot more beefy than he should be. Adaptation Dye-Job: His version of Bumi is blond. The real one has white hair and was a redhead during his youth. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Just like the real Bumi. Fake Muscles: His pecs and guns are obviously part of a costume. They're not even the same color as his skin... either the actor'sorthe real Bumi's.

characters.name: The Blue Spirit
characters.description: A mysterious figure known for his iconic opera mask. With his incredible badassery and excellent stealth skills, he tries to rescue Aang from Admiral Zhao. Badass Normal: The Blue Spirit can hold his own against skilled Benders with just his swords.Zuko never Firebends while in this persona, presumably as a means of protecting his secret identity. Cool Mask: A theater mask depicting the Dark Water Spirit from the playLove Amongst the Dragons. Not only is it a really badass mask,it also helps hide Zuko's identity. The Cowl: Subverted. He freed Aang from Zhao's clutches, butthis was only to capture Aang and get the glory for himself. Dual Wielding: His dual dao swords are so iconic that Zhao can figure out his identity just by seeing them in his room.

characters.name: Player Jet
characters.description: Player Jet, who has spiky hair and chews on a flower, appears in two scenes. In Act I, he floods a village to impress Player Katara, who hugs him and says "Oh Jet, you're so...bad...." In Act II, he appears in Lake Laogai, and is presumed dead when a rock lands on him. He isBrainwashedin that scene, as indicated by googly eyes. Instead of the real Jet's twin hook swords, Player Jet is armed with twin hook hands. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Player Katara certainly does. Anime Hair: His hair, being an exaggeration of the real Jet'sWild Hair. It's long, spiky, and sticks up on its ends. Brainwashed and Crazy: Like the real Jet, except it makes him look far goofier. Character Exaggeration: Like everyone else in the play.

characters.name: Player Earth King
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: Earth King Kuei was left in the dark about Long Feng and the Dai Li's brainwashings and immediately ordered the former arrested upon finding out the truth. This Earth King isresponsiblefor the brainwashing. Composite Character: The playwright either wasn't aware of Long Feng orsimply wanted to simplify things for a shorter play, so the Earth King is the one responsible for Long Feng's brainwashing of Jet. Funny Background Event: His appearance is one, with him being barely visible during the play's depiction of Azula defeating Aang in which we can see the depiction of the Earth King is an incredibly-short man with oversizedNerd Glassessitting in Bosco's lapsitting on his throne. The Napoleon: The real Kuei is on the tall side, but Player Earth King looks child-sized. Nerd Glasses: Compared to Kuei's tiny glasses, the actor for the Earth King briefly glimpsed in the play has oversized glasses.

characters.name: Player Yue
characters.description: Player Yue appears at the end of Act I. She wears a pink dress with many bows, and her hair is a braid attached to her hair loops. When she sacrifices herself to become the Moon Spirit, she is hoisted up on a moon prop, while Player Sokka (and the real one) grieves below. Adaptational Skimpiness: She's wearing a tube dress.In the North Pole. The real Yue was appropriately dressed. Anime Hair: It looks like a giant bow or a pretzel. Ascend to a Higher Plane of Existence: Her "moon duties." Casting Gag: Voiced by Jennie Kwan, who is also the voice of Sokka's girlfriend Suki by the time of the play.

characters.name: Kanna
characters.description: Katara and Sokka's paternal grandmother- or 'Gran-Gran' to her grandkids. Arranged Marriage: With Pakku in the past. Cool Old Lady: Very wise and motherly. Dark and Troubled Past: Was arranged to marry Pakku and ran away because she refused to conform to the Northern Water Tribe's sexism. She then had to see a number of atrocities from the Fire Nation, including the death of her daughter-in-law. And her only son is out fighting in the war. It’s then revealed that in her youth (some time after running away from the North), she personally witnessed the Fire Nation raid the Southern Water Tribe and take all of the water-benders,including her friend Hama. December–December Romance:After so many years separated, she married Pakku when he travelled to the Southern Water Tribe.

characters.name: Kya I
characters.description: Kya was the mother of Sokka and Katara and the wife of Hakoda. Her death during a raid on her home had a profound impact upon both her children. Katara wore her mother's necklace as a memento of her affection. I Am Spartacus: How she saved her daughter's life, as she lied about being the waterbender while her daughter was. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: We see a brief vision of her in Book Two, however when we get a better visual via flashback in Book Three she looks quite a bit different. Good Parents: She's remembered fondly of by both Katara and Sokka, especially the former. Happily Married: Was implied to be this with Hakoda.

characters.name: Chief Arnook
characters.description: The chieftain of the Northern Water Tribe during the final stages of the Hundred Year War. The Good King: Arnook always has people's safety in mind. Horrible Judge of Character: Why he thought an incompetentJerkasslike Hahn would be a suitable match for Yue is anyone's guess. Outliving One's Offspring: Downplayed. His daughter, Yue, sacrifices herself to save the Moon spirit. Yue is now an immortal spirit but cannot readily communicate with her mortal friends and loved ones. Reasonable Authority Figure: Caring for the Northern Water Tribe is his first priority, and is willing to listen to new information from Sokka and takes him at his word that the information is accurate when Sokka points out what they think they know about the Fire Nation is 85 years out of date. He assists the Avatar but is not willing to force Pakku to break tradition and train Katara which could alienate and cause division within the tribe. Additionally, while Arnook does remove Sokka from the mission after his act of disrespect and insubordination and starting a fight with a fellow warrior, he tasks Sokka to protect his daughter instead of sentencing him to a grim punishment as the existential threat makes it clear every warrior needs to be put to good use.

characters.name: Hahn
characters.description: Hahn was a warrior of the Northern Water Tribe and Princess Yue's fiancé. During the Siege of the North, he led a group of Northern Water Tribe soldiers infiltrating the Fire Nation fleet. Accidental Misnaming: He often mispronounces the names of those he is either apathetic to or hates. He pronounces Sokka's name with a long O sound, and when telling Admiral Zhao toPrepare to Die, he calls him AdmiralChoi.noteThough, it's possible that Hahn believes that it's the correct pronunciation of his name, given theIn-Universewriting being Chinese characters. Ambition Is Evil: He's betrothed to Princess Yue because of the political perks, and this is portrayed as a negative aspect. Arranged Marriage: With Princess Yue. Unlike most examples, he doesn't even hide that he has no love for her, and while bragging about it outright states he is doing it for political advantages. Asshole Victim: Zhao chucks him off his ship. He is never seen again.

characters.name: Jet
characters.description: As a young boy, Jet's family was killed by the Fire Nation. Swearing vengeance, Jet became a dashing rebel against their forces, forming aMerry-Men esquegroup of freedom fighters with other war orphans. However, Jet has an extremist side and is willing to destroy the Fire Nation by any means necessary. After getting called out by Katara and Sokka, Jet realized the error of his ways and tried to start over, only to get brainwashed into an agent of the Dai Li by Long Feng. And then is killed by him when he tried to break free. Ambiguous Situation:It's not clear if the poisoned dagger he showed to the Gaang belongs to the old man or not. Though given that Jet had no qualms with lying to Katara and Aang in order to get their unwitting help in flooding the Fire Nation occupied village, the possibility that he was lying about the dagger is high.While it's possible that Jet telling Smellerbee and Duke to take Sokka on a "long walk" is meant to keep him from warning Aang and Katara about his flood plan until then, it could also be aDeadly Euphemismto have Sokka quietly killed, given his willingness to sacrifice any life needed to take down the Fire Nation. It's not clear if the poisoned dagger he showed to the Gaang belongs to the old man or not. Though given that Jet had no qualms with lying to Katara and Aang in order to get their unwitting help in flooding the Fire Nation occupied village, the possibility that he was lying about the dagger is high. While it's possible that Jet telling Smellerbee and Duke to take Sokka on a "long walk" is meant to keep him from warning Aang and Katara about his flood plan until then, it could also be aDeadly Euphemismto have Sokka quietly killed, given his willingness to sacrifice any life needed to take down the Fire Nation. Anti-Hero: Albeit a tragic one. At first, he seems like a romantic, handsome, vigilante freedom fighter, but he's willing to go to horrifying extremes to defeat the Fire Nation. Later, he goes straight.Unfortunately,

characters.name: The Freedom Fighters
characters.description: The Freedom Fighters are a handful of children and teenagers from (apparently) all over the Earth Kingdom who have been orphaned by the attacks of the Fire Nation. Led by Jet, they are aRagtag Bunch of Misfitswho pretty much throw monkey wrenches into Fire Nation activity wherever they can. Longshot and Smellerbee show up with Jet en route to Ba Sing Se in Book Two. Pipsqueak and The Duke show up in Season 3. Sneers, Smellerbee, and Longshot reappeared inThe Promiseleading the reorganized Freedom Fighters. Alliterative Name: TheFreedomFighters. The Atoner: Longshot and Smellerbee have truly changed by the time of Season 2. They go from blindly following Jet's orders to giving him advice about his actions. When they find out Jet was brainwashed by the Dai Li, they help Team Avatar undo it and fight to rescue Appa. Badass Normal: Longshot and Smellerbee can hold their own against Dai Li Earthbenders. As Freedom Fighters though, we can assume that anti-Firebender combat is something of a specialty for them.

characters.name: Cai the Cabbage Merchant
characters.description: A hapless cabbage merchant whose produce keeps getting inadvertently destroyed by the Gaang. Needless to say, he's not too fond of them. Ascended Extra: At first, he was just a funny background character, but he proved so popular that he got a New York Comic Con-exclusive Funko Pop of himself (complete with cabbage cart), a Youtooz figure, starred in his own picture book, andbecame Vaatu'sDragoninAvatar Legends: The Fighting Game. Butt-Monkey: Bar none, the biggestschlimazelin the entire franchise; the poor little fella just wants to make a sale... Catchphrase: He tends to shriek, "MY CABBAGES!!!" nearly every time his produce is destroyed. A Day in the Limelight: In 2024, he stars in his own picture book, appropriately titledMy Cabbages!

characters.name: The Kyoshi Warriors
characters.description: An all-female team of warriors who serve as the protectors of Kyoshi Island. Later, they fight for the Earth Kingdom during the war and serve as Zuko's bodyguards. Action Girl: All of them, especially Suki and eventuallyTy Lee. Amazon Brigade: They are an all-female group of warriors. Avatar Kyoshi originally founded the group so the women of her village would know how to protect themselves but eventually became a force to protect Kyoshi Island from intruders. Anti-Magic:Ty Lee teaches them chi-blocking in prison. Art Evolution: In their first appearance, all the Warriors besides Suki pretty much looked identical. In subsequent appearances, each Kyoshi Warrior has a unique face shape, hairstyle, and headpiece.

characters.name: Foamy Mouth Guy
characters.description: A fan of the Avatar who lives on Kyoshi Island. Known for his tendency to go into a screaming fit and foam at the mouth when he thinks Aang is near. All There in the Manual:Word of Godhas statedSukiused to date him, and is not proud of it. Creator Cameo: He's voiced by series co-creatorBryan Konietzko. Hero-Worshipper:Absolutely adoresAang. Loony Fan: He faints and foams in the mouth when Aang is near.

characters.name: June
characters.description: A skilled bounty hunter, June is out for money and doesn't care who she has to work for to get it. She collects bounties with Nyla, her pet Shirshu, a ferocious beast with an incredible sense of smell. When she inadvertently damaged Zuko's ship while chasing a bounty, Zuko had her hunt the Avatar as compensation. In the finale, she was recruited by Zuko to track down Iroh. Animal Motifs: AnIn-UniverseMix-and-Match Crittercalled a shirshu, which is averycompetent tracker that can paralyze prey with a swipe of its tongue. Fitting for a dangerous bounty hunter like her. Back for the Finale:She comes back in Sozin's Comet to help the Gaang find Aang. When that fails, she is instead asked to find Iroh, and successfully does. Badass Normal: She isn't known to have any bending abilities, but kicks plenty of ass with her whip and pet Shirshu. Bar Brawl: She spends her free time beating up burly men.

characters.name: Nyla
characters.description: Action Pet: For June, as they do bounty hunting together. All Animals Are Dogs: Zigzagged. Nyla is a combination of ananteater, wolf, and mole. He also does some dog-like things, such as licking when being friendly and growling when angry. Big Friendly Dog: Zigzagged. Friendly to June but dangerous to those their hunting, whether they're a good person or not. Eyeless Face: As a shirshu, Nyla doesn't have any eyes. Gender-Blender Name: "Nyla" is a girls' name butthisNyla is male.

characters.name: The Pirate Captain
characters.description: The Pirate Captain and his crew first appear in the first season episode "The Waterbending Scroll". Aang and his friends come aboard their ship to browse and Katara steals a very valuable waterbending scroll that The Pirate captain said he had gotten "at a most reasonable price, free" Afterwards the pirates chase after Aang and his friends to take the scroll back, they escape, then the pirates team up with Prince Zuko who is hunting The Avatar. At first The Pirates and Zuko work well together as they manage to catch Aang and his friends but then Sokka convinces the pirates to renege on their deal with Prince Zuko at which point aMêlée à Troisbattle ensues, Aang and his friends manage to escape. The Pirates ship and Prince Zuko's River Boat get destroyed in the process, and the pirates are not seen again until "The Waterbending Master" in which Admiral Zhao hires them to kill Prince Zuko. After that they are not seen again. Badass Normal: The Pirate Captain is skilled enough with a sword to take on Prince Zuko. "Blackmail" Is Such an Ugly Word: He admits that he stole the waterbending scroll from a northern water tribe member, but doesn't call it as such. Faux Affably Evil: The Pirate Captain appears very personable if somewhat gruff and rough around the edges, but he drops all pretenses if he thinks you're wasting his time. Honest John's Dealership: The pirates' ships main purpose when at port is as a store selling exotic curios.

characters.name: Oh
characters.description: Affably Evil: He seems genuinely nice, even if it is very apparent that he's quite a shady character, he also comes across as somewhat chatty and annoying. Badass Normal: The Pirate Barker knows how to use his weapons and isn't afraid to let them do the talking if the need arises. "Blackmail" Is Such an Ugly Word: When Sokka deduces and screams out that "You guys are pirates!" The Pirate Barker says "We prefer to think of ourselves as 'high risk traders'." Combat Pragmatist: Uses smoke pellets to distract and disorient his enemies. Equal-Opportunity Evil: When he's barking about their items, he mentions that "Earth Nation, Water Nation, and Fire Nation" citizens are all welcome in his shop. He'salsoequally interested in stealing from any of them.

characters.name: Zei
characters.description: Professor Zei was the head of the Anthropology Department at Ba Sing Se University. An ambitious cultural anthropologist, he was well-traveled and highly educated in exotic cultures. His thirst for knowledge brought him to strange, remote, and often dangerous places. Zei was an eccentric man to whom knowledge was priceless. He got very excited at the prospect of learning anything about history or the world around him. A map of his travels showed he had been everywhere in the world, except the Fire Nation. Even though he had discovered many lost civilizations over the years, he longed to find the "crown jewel" of ancient discoveries: Wan Shi Tong's Library. He never managed to find Wan Shi Tong's Library until he ran into Aang and his friends in the Si Wong Desert. He explained to them that he made several expeditions into the desert but almost died each time. He finally fulfills his life long wish, by flying on the back of Appa. After they get into Wan Shi Tong's Library, Wan Shi Tong initially refuses them entry , but lets them pass under the condition that they provide him with new knowledge. Unlike Aang and his friends who wanted to use Wan Shi Tong's library to help them find possible ways to help them defeat the Fire Nation, Professor Zei wanted to find the library simply because he was a lover of knowledge. When Wan Shi Tong finds out about this, he sinks his library into the desert sand and tries to keep Aang and his friends trapped for eternity. Professor Zei willingly chooses to stay behind, and inThe Legend of Korrait's revealed that he died there. Adventure Archaeologist: Professor Zei divides his time teaching Cultural Anthropology at Ba Sing Se University and looking for lost civilizations. Adventurer Outfit: It helps him survive in the hostile desert. Badass Bookworm: We never actually see how much of a badass he is, but he has to be one to have journeyed through the Si Wong Desert several times and live to tell the tale.

characters.name: Song
characters.description: A young girl who worked at a hospital in an agricultural Earth Kingdom village. Disappeared Dad: Justified, while her dad isn't living with Song and her mother, it's because he was captured by the Fire Nation during a raid when Song was a little girl. The Farmer and the Viper: She unknowingly takes Zuko, the banished prince of the Fire Nation to stay at her place for the night. He ends up stealing her ostrich-horse. Good Scars, Evil Scars: She has a large scar on her leg from being burned by a firebender. The Medic: Downplayed, Song works in a hospital, but the only medical skill she's shown is when she applies ointment to Iroh's rash after he's drunk tea made from a poisonous plant.

characters.name: Yung
characters.description: An aggressive commander of the Omashu military. The Remnant: Yung refuses to surrender with Bumi and goes into the sewers to fight back against the Fire Nation occupiers. What Happened to the Mouse?: Aang convinces him and his men to leave the city and fight another day but they never return in the show.

characters.name: Lee
characters.description: A village boy whom Zuko encounters while wandering alone. Broken Pedestal: He likes Zuko and sees him as a friend until finding out he's the Fire Nation prince. Conscription: He's temporarily taken as a conscript by the local soldiers after threatening one with a knife when they rob his family. One-Steve Limit: Zuko had previously used the alias "Lee" when staying with Song, and sticks with that alias in Ba Sing Se long after meeting this Lee. Small Role, Big Impact: Zuko only meets him once while travelling through his village, but Lee's rejection of Zuko after he reveals his true identity is his first time truly reckoning with what the Fire Nation means to the rest of the world, and the propaganda he was raised on about the war.

characters.name: Chin
characters.description: A brutal Earthbending warlord from Avatar Kyoshi's era. Asshole Victim: Aside from Chin Village, everyone believed that Chin's death (even if it was technically accidental by Kyoshi) was well-deserved due to his being a brutal conqueror. Even if Kyoshi did see Chin's death as manslaughter on her part, she still wouldn't feel guilty over how he died, given who he is. While Aang preferred that the man not die, so he could face consequences, he clearly doesn't care for Chin other than using his accidental death to argue against Kyoshi's opinion that she "killed" him. Base-Breaking Character:In-Universe. To the Gaang, Avatar Kyoshi, and the rest of the world, Chin was a brutal conqueror who needed to be stopped (though Aang prefers that he shouldn't die) in Avatar Kyoshi's era. While Chin Village still venerates him as a great leader in the present, they see his death by Avatar Kyoshi as unjustified. Disney Villain Death: He fell to his own doom by refusing to move away from the falling cliff. Fatal Flaw: Unsurprisingly,Prideand stubborness. After Kyoshi embarrasses him by stripping him down to his underwear and using the Avatar State to literally move Kyoshi Island away from the mainland, thus denying his conquest, Chin had aVillainous Breakdownthat prevented him from moving out of the way of the falling cliff.

characters.name: Lao and Poppy Beifong
characters.description: Toph's parents. Although they both love Toph dearly, they failed to recognize what their daughter really wanted, believing her blindness made her weak, helpless, and frail. As a result, they had her guarded and cared for the majority of the time. Unbeknownst to both of them, Toph had become an excellent earthbender all on her own. When Toph runs away to teach Aang earthbending, Lao hires Xin Fu and Yu to bring her back. Abusive Parents: Mostly out ofneglectand overprotectiveness. They locked Toph in the house, ostensibly to protect their helpless, blind daughter, but they still continue this behavior even after she proves strong and capable. Then, after Toph runs away, they hire two people to bring her back, one of whom had kidnapped her moments ago. Aerith and Bob: Poppy's name stands out compared to her husband's and daughter's Chinese names. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Despite disowning her in "The Rift" Lao is seen keeping a picture of Toph, showing that for all his disappointment in her, he does care. Because I Said So: "That's just how it's done." was Lao's typical response to Toph's questions, which became a source of great discomfort for her.

characters.name: The Boulder
characters.description: An arrogant yet entertaining Earthbender, he was a wrestler and arena champion who thought he would easily defeat a certain little girl in the tournament. He was painfully curb stomped instead. The Big Guy: Just not as big as the Big Bad Hippo. Boisterous Bruiser: To the point that he's aThird-Person Person. The Brute: The Boulder is very strong, and is an excellent earth bender, but when Katara says that he could be a possible Earthbending teacher to Aang, Aang reminds her "That Bumi told me to find somebody who listens to the earth, he's just listening to his big muscles." Curb-Stomp Battle: To establish Toph's badassery, The Boulder gets hit with aGroin Attackbefore being catapulted out of the ring.

characters.name: The Big Bad Hippo
characters.description: The Big Bad Hippo was an Earthbending wrestler in Earth Runble VI, just like the Boulder. He almost beat the Boulder by stomping his feet and jumping up and down, which caused him to almost fall out of the ring. This was the Hippo's signature move which was called "Rocking The Boat". The Boulder however manages to catch his balance and defeats the Hippo by lifting him up in the air using his Earthbending and tossing him out of the ring. Angry, Angry Hippos: He's not a literal hippopotamus, but he's a massive Earthbending wrestler who happens to look like one. Animal Motifs: Fitting his wrestling name, he is big, bulky, and has a large mouth with tusk-like teeth like an actual hippopotamus. Boisterous Bruiser: Exactly the personality you'd expect from an earthbender. Boring, but Practical: Hippo's primary strategy for getting the Boulder out of the ring...is to use Earthbending to tilt the entire ring in an attempt to off-balance the Boulder and make him stumble out. To Hippo's credit, it nearly works.

characters.name: The Earth Rumble VI Wrestlers
characters.description: Earthbenders participating in the Earth Rumble VI earthbending tournament, where they get beaten by The Boulder. Later they kidnap Toph and Aang, and get curbstomped by Toph for their troubles. After that, they're never seen again. Butt-Monkey: He gets easily defeated whenever he fights; during Earth Rumble VI, the Boulder sends him flying before he takes a step. Then he's the first of the competitors to be defeated during their fight with Toph in the climax, and as each is thrown out of the ring, they land on him. Contractual Genre Blindness: Pauses upon entering the arena to sing the Fire Nation national anthem, only to be interrupted and beaten by the Boulder. Presumably, this is part of his shtick as aForeign Wrestling Heel, making the Fire Nation look silly by having Fire Nation patriotism be the cause of his swift defeat. Curb-Stomp Battle: The Boulder beats him before he has the chance to attack. He doesslightlybetter with Toph in that he gets an attack out-anattack, singular, before she blows him out of the arena. Fake Nationality: In-universe. Despite his entire character, he's an earthbender- and while the comics show that there are a few Fire Nation-loyal Earthbenders in the colonies, Fire Nation Man is shown sandbending, an art used mostly in the desert, which is still part of the Earth Kingdom, so he's almost certainly an Earth Kingdom national.

characters.name: Xin Fu and Yu
characters.description: Xin Fu is the coordinator of the wrestling tournament in which Toph participates. When he thinks Toph cheated him out of the prize money he offered for her defeat, he kidnaps her and demands the prize money back as ransom. Yu is an Earthbending teacher in Toph's hometown. He was hired to teach Toph Earthbending, but he grossly underestimated her abilities and thought she would never get past the beginner level. Both of them are later hired by Toph's father to bring her back after she ran away with Team Avatar. Affably Evil: Master Yu, who is very polite and softspoken for a bad guy. Allegorical Character: Yu is one for strip mall dojo's and their blatant attempts to net more money from their 'students' rather than actuallyteachthem martial arts. Doubles as aTake That!.

characters.name: Sha-Mo
characters.description: Everyone Has Standards: He yells, "WHAT DID YOU DO?!" at his son when he finds out he stole the Avatar's sky bison to sell him to poachersandstranded a group of innocent people in the desert. It turns out he wasn't part of the theft and believes that violatingSacred Hospitalityis awful. Reasonable Authority Figure: The Chief seemed to have no part in the theft, and while figuring out what had happened, mentions they should offer the Gaang hospitality. Unfortunately, Aang is too far gone to listen to him. Sacred Hospitality: Believes strongly in this. Since the next episode shows the Gaang no longer in the desert, he presumably made good on his word and escorted them safely out along with giving them supplies, though unfortunately he couldn't return Appa as his idiot son had already sold the bison.

characters.name: Ghashiun
characters.description: Desert Bandits: He leads a group of thieves who ambush desert travelers and steal their belongings. Hypocrite: He tears down the Gaang for supposedly stealing a sandbender ship, when he’s the one who stole Appa from them. Not only that, it turns outhe also stole that very shipfrom another tribe. Toph almost immediately recognizes him as the thief while he denies his wrongdoings, and this wasbeforeshe reveals herself as aLiving Lie Detector. Mugging the Monster: He didnotknow he was stealing the Avatar'sLiving Emotional Crutch, and comes dangerously close to getting murdered by a pissed-off Avatar State Aang. Oh, Crap!: When he realizes that the bison he stole belonged to the now enraged Avatar, and they have no way of getting him back. Suspiciously Specific Denial: Ghashiun immediately gets defensive when Katara explains that their bison was stolen, denying that they had any part of it. As his father points out, nobody accused them of anything.

characters.name: Long Feng
characters.description: In the Earth Kingdom capital of Ba Sing Se, a group called the Dai Li keeps the war with the Fire Nation a secret, in order to maintain cultural order. A man who has fought long and hard for his position, Long Feng serves as theirBig Brother-likeleader. Using the Dai Li to keep himself in power, Long Feng manipulates both the city and the Earth King himself, whom Long Feng uses as a puppet ruler. After getting exposed by the Gaang, he tried to get back in power by working with Azula and double-crossing her at the moment of triumph. That didn't work out too hot. Arc Villain: For the latter half of Book Two up until the end, where Azulashows him who's boss. Arrogance Breeds Laziness: Implied. Long Feng came from a humble background before clawing his way up the social ladder, becoming theEvil Chancellorof Ba Sing Se long before the Gaang came into the picture. However, it's implied that after spending years of being the top dog of aState Sec, it causes Long Feng to fully believe in his own hype and that he can manipulate and handle any threat that comes his way, which leads to his downfall by Azula's gambits. Bald of Evil: He's anEvil Chancellorwho wears his hair in aqueue, which involves keeping the front half of the head shaved. Beard of Evil: Similar to theBald of Evil, he has a Fu Manchu-esque beard to highlight him as an antagonist.

characters.name: The Dai Li
characters.description: The secretive and elite police force of Ba Sing Se who work to capture, interrogate, and imprison political dissidents. The organization was founded by Avatar Kyoshi with the aim of "protecting the cultural heritage of Ba Sing Se", effectively protecting the Earth King's interest against subversive individuals and groups. Big Fish in a Bigger Ocean: They're highly capable as a police force, but their insistence on there being no war in Ba Sing Se has meant that they have no real wartime experience and are at something of a loss when it comes to facing those who do, like Team Avatar and Azula. Their training clearly isn't meant for direct and open combat, with their signature earth gloves being most often used to ambush and immobilize targets and for stealth purposes (allowing them to wall-cling and therefore hide and attack from unexpected directions). They're still no slouches in direct fights, but they're nothing special either. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: When the Earth King busts Long Feng for lying about the war, the Dai Liplan a coup to make him the leader. Then Azula comes, and they switch loyalties to her. It's lampshadedby Azula herself in the midst of her paranoidVillainous Breakdownwhen she banishes them, noting that they've betrayed their previous masters so why should she expect anything better if someone came along with an offer? Connections Are Not Power: Their status as a police force does nothing to keep those more powerful than them from putting them in their place, especially since the Dai Li never had any experience in war.By the end of the series, even siding with Azula did not prevent her from exiling them. Dark Is Evil: Wear dark green robes and are a corrupt force in Ba Sing Se.

characters.name: Joo Dee
characters.description: Team Avatar's guide and chaperone in Ba Sing Se. Brainwashed and Crazy: Brainwashed by the Dai Li to act as their spy. The Dreaded: The citizens of Ba Sing Se fear the Joo Dees as being representatives of the Dai Lee and refuse to have anything to do with anyone accompanying one. Merchants immediately close up shop when Team Avatar appears with her. Hope Spot: When Aang blows up at her and slams a door in her face, it seems to break her brainwashing. Our Joo Dee's crying as she explains to Long Feng that the children no longer trust her. Then Long Feng reactivates it without blinking an eye. Not So Stoic: Out of all the Joo Dees, this one doesn't always act like a mindless state drone, which means she has some level of resistance if it takes a shock to bring her out of it. She breaks out of her fake smile after seeing Aang and his friends make a spectacle to see the King, showing genuine concern for them and implores them to leave the palace immediately. Then, after Aang yells in her face, she's outright intimidated, and she criesright in front of her boss, clearly fearing Long Feng will have her head for her failure.

characters.name: Jin
characters.description: Jin is a citizen of Ba Sing Se and a regular patron of the tea shop where Iroh and Zuko work. She nurses a crush on Zuko and decides to ask him out on a date, which doesn't go very well. She appeared in one of theAvatarmagazine comics that came out between Seasons 2 and 3 and had a two-second cameo in the first episode of the third season. Despite her very short screen time,she has gained a decent measure of popularity with the fandom.Years later, she made a surprising return as the main character ofCity of Echoes, the first entry of theAvatar Legendssub-series of novels. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Inverted. She has no idea who her date really is and only sees Zuko's cute side. Ascended Extra/A Day in the Limelight:City of Echoesgreatly expands on her character and backstory, retells the events from “The Tale of Zuko” and her other brief appearances from her perspective, and reveals that she had her own adventures opposing both Long Feng’s government and, later, the Fire Nation occupiers. Big Eater: Subverted. While watching her eat her food on their date, Zuko says she has a big appetite for a girl, but she never eats any particularly large amount of food, and this comment is just Zuko's painfully awkward, harebrained attempt to make conversation with her. Breakout Character: She's popular enough to star in her own role as the main viewpoint character ofCity of Echoes.

characters.name: Hei Bai
characters.description: A forest spirit, normally appearing in the form of a large, docile panda. He served as the protector of the forest on the edge of Senlin Village for a millenium, until the forest was reduced to a pile of ash. Outraged, Hei Bai assumed that it had been done by the residents of Senlin Village, and began attacking the village every night. Anti-Villain: Hei Bai really isn't a malevolant spirit. He's just angry that his home was destroyed and started taking out his anger on the village he thought was responsible. Once he learns the truth, he lets them all go. Beary Friendly: Despite his ability to transform into a four-armed monster, Hei Bai is actually not really that malicious. Beware the Nice Ones: Hei Bai is one of the more gentle spirits who prefers to keep to himself. However, when enraged, he transforms into a horrifying, four-armed monster capable of destroying everything in his path. Breath Weapon:He roars a massive blue wavethat can easily blast buildings apart and blast people back, though there's some ambiguity if it's an actualBreath Weaponor if he's just roaring loudly and the color is for the audience's sake.

characters.name: Tui and La
characters.description: Awakening the Sleeping Giant: Tui and La are very powerful spirits, but they're mostly busy keeping the tides and such in order and don't care about the war.Then Zhao kills Tui, and a pissed-off La goes Koizilla and takes revenge by utterly annihilating Zhao's invasion fleet. Benevolent Abomination: Albeit ones who spend most of their time looking fairly harmless. They're among the most ancient and powerful of spirits and are the patrons of the Water Tribes. Beware the Nice Ones: They're fairly benevolent as spirits go, and La at least is willing to do Aang a favor on request. They are still, however, piscine personifications of the moon and ocean and theoriginalwaterbenders.La demonstrates that they arenotto be taken lightly when Zhao kills Tui, fusing with Aang to singlehandedly annihilate Zhao's entire fleet in revenge. Even then, La is discriminatory in attacking, making sure to not catch any Water Tribe members in its waves and halting once the moon returns. Dragged Off to Hell: La does thisto Zhao, grabbing him, taking him into the Spirit World, and dumping him in the Fog of Lost Souls to punish him for Tui's death. Lord of the Ocean: They are the personifications of the moon and the ocean and represent the eternal push and pull of the tides, having taken the form of two black and white koi fish within the Spirit Oasis in the North Pole. WhenTui is killed by Zhao to rob the Waterbenders of their bending ability, La retaliates by fusing with Aang in the Avatar state to become a massive water spirit, rampaging across the North Pole and decimating the Fire Nation armada effortlessly.

characters.name: Koh
characters.description: One of the oldest spirits in the Spirit World, Koh is a nightmarish centipede creature with a dangerous hobby of stealing faces. If he sees a face that makes even the slightest twitch of emotion, he will snatch it off and wear it as his own. Although he was attacked by Avatar Kuruk, he holds no grudge against the other Avatars. Because of his age, he is privy to many secrets of the world around him. So if Aang comes knocking on his door for help, who is he to refuse?There's always room for one more... He only appears in one episode (three technically, but the other two were a flashback to that episode and a cameo), and barely does anything, but he's so damn creepy that everyone remembers him. Animalistic Abomination: A huge face-stealing abomination that looks like a (mostly) human-faced centipede. Koh has more than human faces in the bag, though. Antagonistic Offspring: To theMother of Faces. She says they had a major fallout at the beginning of time. Anti-Villain: His actions suggest that he's simply amoral, not pure evil. He stole the face of Avatar Kuruk's lover to punish him for his arrogance, and bears no ill will towards Aang or any other incarnation of the Avatar for Kuruk's attack on him because he knows they're not the same person. Furthermore, he willingly told Aang the locations of the Ocean and Moon Spirits and the danger they were in, albeit in a cryptic and riddle-filled manner and while constantly trying to steal his face.

characters.name: Lian
characters.description: A main character fromthe video game. She was captured by the Fire Nation and used to make powerful machines to aid them in the war. Arc Villain:She turns out to be the main antagonist in the video game. Canon Foreigner: Lian was introduced in the first video game adaptation of the show, and as such, is not part of the actual canon of the series. Continuity Nod: Considering the anti-bender Equalist Movement that would occur inThe Legend of Korra, one could say Lian is a kind of predecessor to the idea of non-benders using machinery to assert dominance over benders due to mistreatment. Damsel in Distress: In the "Amongst the Enemy" chapter, she's the Fire Nation's prisoner, being used to make machines for the Fire Nation.

characters.name: Yu Dao Resistance
characters.description: A group trying to prevent Yu Dao from being taken back by the Earth Kingdom. Conflicting Loyalty: Most of the Yu Dao Resistance feel loyalty to their city, a Fire Nation colony, rather than having their relatives and friends expelled by the Earth Kingdom. Dishing Out Dirt: Kori and her three cousins are earthbenders. Fighting for a Homeland: Yu Dao has been a Fire Nation colony for generations, long enough that everyone there, though descended from Fire Nationals, have lived there for their whole lives and consider it home and the Fire Nation proper to be foreign, hence the resistance. Though the century-long war has caused enmity with the Earth Kingdom and Team Avatar, who wish for the original territories to be restored butthe concept of dual-citizenship and naturalization are unknown to them until Katara pointed them out. La Résistance: They push to prevent Yu Dao from being taken by the Earth Kingdom.

characters.name: Toph's Metalbending Students
characters.description: A group of kids Toph noticed hadmetalbendingpotential, and brought them in to train. Badass Crew: They start evolving into this over the course of the comics. Big, Thin, Short Trio: Ho-Tun, The Dark One, and Penga are big, thin and short, respectively. The Bus Came Back: After having last appeared inToph Beifong's Metalbending Academy, they make cameo appearances for the first time in an animated project inAvatar Aang: The Last Airbender, nearly five years later. Chekhov's Skill: Penga tries to impress Toph by showing her ability to spin helmets with metalbending, though her teacher is not impressed. When the trio joins the fight at Yu Dao, Penga saves Toph's life by blinding the Fire Nation soldiers with their own helmets.

characters.name: Master Kunyo
characters.description: A pretentious firebending teacher from Yu Dao. He was previously an instructor for the Royal Family before being sent away for his inadequacies in teachingAzula. Allegorical Character: He represents the evils of colonialism. Everyoneelseinvolved in the conflict issympathetic; Aang just wants to set things right after the war, Kuei wants to beThe Good Kingand stand up for his subjects, Zuko doesn't want to break up families, and the colonials themselves are portrayed as victims of the past generations' crimes and currently stuck between a rock (the Fire Nation keeping the land it stole and the system that prioritized Fire Nation descendants) and a hard place (breaking up interracial families and deporting descendants of fire nationals to a country they'd likely never evenvisitedand didn't really consider their own). Kunyo? He's a racist prick whose goals are colonialism at its worst in miniature, and he gets cathartically beaten back by the 'natives' of the dojo he took from Toph. Butt-Monkey: In his first appearance, Toph metalbends a spear around his head, and a flashback inThe Searchestablishes that Azula set his pants on fire when she disagreed with him about firebending forms. Fantastic Racism: Calls Toph a 'Dirt Person' and Sokka a 'Snow Savage'. Not Helping Your Case: It doesn't come to anything in-comic because everyone has more important things to worry about, but he writes a letter to Fire Lord Zuko about the "dirt person" and "snow savage" who took over his dojo- with the people he referred to with racial slurs being Zuko's close friends Sokka and Toph.

characters.name: Ikem
characters.description: Ursa's lover when they were both simply members of the Hira'a acting troupe, before they were separated when Azulon came to marry Ursa to his son Ozai. Badass Normal: Gets the better of a firebending soldier with nothing but wooden prop swords. Beard of Sorrow: Grows one after Ursa is forced to accept Ozai's proposal. Break His Heart to Save Him: Ursa tells him that she "joyfully accepted" Ozai's proposal to stop his attempts to resist, which would almost certainly get him killed. Chekhov's Gunman: Hey, remember that nice family from Part 2, Noren, Noriko, and Kiyi?Noriko is actually Ursa with a new face and no memory of her royal life, and Noren is Ikem with a new face. Kiyi? Meet Zuko's half-sister he never knew about.

characters.name: Rafa and Misu
characters.description: A brother and sister pair the Gaang meets in the Forgotten Forest, they have been waiting for the Mother Of Faces for a year to make a request. Action Girl: Misu. She even developed her own offensive waterbending technique, since being a woman in the North Tribe she couldn't learn regular offensive waterbending. Big Sister Instinct: Misu spent decades trying to heal Rafa's face. Brother–Sister Team: Rafa with his sister, Misu, who wants to heal his face. Determinator: Misu in finding a way to heal her brother's face.

characters.name: The Mother of Faces
characters.description: A powerful spirit who makes all the faces in the world. Once a year, she comes to the Forgotten Forest, and will fulfill one request. Eldritch Abomination: She may be a somewhat benign example when she feels like it, but she definitely looks the part. She is the source of all human faces, being the one that gave humans individual identity to begin with. Everyone Has Standards:Even she dislikes Koh's face stealing, which makes her more reasonable in granting a new face to someone for free if their face was stolen by him. Godzilla Threshold: She's strict on her "one request per season" rule,but if she finds someone who lost their face because of Koh, she will unconditionally restore that face. Luke, I Am Your Father:Is revealed to be Koh the Face Stealer's mother. He steals faces because his mother crafts them, a fact that she wasn't aware of that leads her to fashion a new face to Rafa anyway as it is her form of atonement for her son's crimes.

characters.name: New Ozai Society
characters.description: Black Shirts: The group were an organization dedicated to freeing Ozai, who had been depowered and imprisoned, replaced by his son Zuko, to reinstate him and remove the "impostor" that was his son Zuko. Curb-Stomp Battle: The entire society didn't stand a chance against Mai, but their defeat was short-lived, and they're back on their feet by the timeSmoke and Shadowrolls around. Doomed by Canon: By the time we see the Fire Nation again inThe Legend of Korra, it’s led by Zuko’s daughter, who took over after her father abdicated. There’s also the fact that we don’t see a single member in sight. Early-Bird Cameo: They first appear in the free comicRebound, which focuses on Mai. In the comicSmoke and Shadow, both Mai and the Ozai Society return. Foregone Conclusion: ByThe Legend of Korra, Zuko has a long rule over the Fire Nation with his daughter taking over afterward. So safe to say, they never bring back the old regime, and they will have fallen apart by then.

characters.name: The Air Acolytes
characters.description: Once they were merely an Avatar Aang fan club, but duringThe Promise, after helping Aang quell the trouble in Yu Dao and showing him that they are trying to keep Air Nomad culture alive, he renames them the Air Acolytes. In theThe Rift, three of them (Xing Ying, Yee-li, and Jingbo) join the Gaang in helping Aang to recreate the Yangchen Festival. Ascended Extra: They get to haveA Day in the LimelightinThe Rift, alongside Aang, after their introduction inThe Promise. Badass Normal: InThe Promise, they fought both sides of the Yu Dao revolution and were more than a match for anyone. InThe Rift, however, they do not do much fighting, mainly because Aang won't let them. Bald Mystic:Downplayed; Xing Ying shaved the front half of her head to imitate the style of Avatar Yangchen and the Air Nomad nuns. Car Fu: Jingbo uses a forklift to try and take out one of the Rough Rhinos, but is stopped from "squishing" him by Xing Ying and Yee-Li.

characters.name: Satoru
characters.description: The current supervisor of a joint Fire Nation and Earth Kingdom mining operation. Ambiguously Related: He has a hairstyle similar to Toph's daughter Lin fromThe Legend of Korra, which hints that he may or may not be her biological father. The age difference between the two doesn't help, either. Call-Forward:Satoru has invented an assembly line process based entirely on machines that non-benders can use, clearly the beginning of the more mechanized world seen inKorra. At the end of Part 3, the Cabbage Merchant, who will go on to found an automobile company, expresses interest in his forklift.His name also has a suspiciously similar resemblance toAsamiandHiroshi Sato, making him a possible ancestor. HisHold Your HippogriffsCatchphraseis even "Flying Fire Ferrets!" Satoru has invented an assembly line process based entirely on machines that non-benders can use, clearly the beginning of the more mechanized world seen inKorra. At the end of Part 3, the Cabbage Merchant, who will go on to found an automobile company, expresses interest in his forklift. His name also has a suspiciously similar resemblance toAsamiandHiroshi Sato, making him a possible ancestor. HisHold Your HippogriffsCatchphraseis even "Flying Fire Ferrets!"

characters.name: Nutha and Niyok
characters.description: A pair of sisters from the Southern Water Tribe who were friends with Katara and Sokka before the two left with Aang. Katara meets the two as they are working at Loban's refinery. Colour-Coded for Your Convenience: Both wear blue scarves with their gray uniforms, identifying them as Water Tribesmen. Death Glare: Nutha's introduction is giving Katara a none-too-friendly stare before yelling at Niyok to return to her side. Fallen-on-Hard-Times Job: The sisters had to leave the Southern Water Tribe and work in a dangerous mine just to eat. Green-Eyed Monster: Nutha seems to be envious of Katara's globetrotting.

characters.name: Loban
characters.description: Lao Beifong's business partner and Satoru's uncle. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He isrunning a hidden iron mine underneath the legit crystal one. Even without the possibility of ticking off a powerful spirit, it's polluting the river and could potentially collapse the entire town. Death by Materialism: Just narrowly subverted;after he finds the iron mask of General Old Iron in his unstable iron mine, he gets Kachi and Vachir and their komodo rhinos to haul it to the Fire Nation, but when General Old Iron arrives, he gets pulled up by the floating mask, with Satoru and Sokka holding onto him. Katara saves them by making a water slide, and Satoru telling Loban to let go to safety. Evil Uncle: Although he took in his nephew Satoru to help run his refinery, he was still verbally abusive to him, particularly after the Gaang paid a visit, with Toph busting one of their malfunctioning machines, angrily blaming him for what happened.It's even revealed that he was digging his own iron mine without anyone's knowledge, nearly endangering their workers, to Lao's fury. Thankfully, he gets better. Fat Bastard: He is verbally abusive towards his nephew Satoru and doesn't give a crap about his workers' safety, to the point ofrunning an unstable iron mine behind his business partner's back.

characters.name: Lady Tienhai
characters.description: A spirit who used to tend the seashore. Bodyguard Crush: Implied with General Old Iron, who protected and was friends with Lady Tienhai. Death Is Cheap: At the end of Part 3, she tells Aang that while a spirit in human form will die, it just means they will go back to being a spirit, though it may take a bit of time to return to their original power. Humans Are Special: She loves humans and is fascinated by their creative potential and was very happy to have a human settlement spring up by her shoreline, because she felt that her beach was beautiful but stagnant. She sometimes took human form to interact with them, and during one of those sojurns she fell in love with a human and decided to stay with him for an entire human life. Interspecies Romance: Fell in love with and married a human who lived by her seashore.

characters.name: Master Boma
characters.description: An older man chaperoning Yangchen, who promised the Air Nomad nuns that he would look after her.
